basis: Tinker: prefill tokens counted by the scripts (priming 54k, $0.011; trajectory over the saves 44k, $0.009; marker contexts 101k, $0.020; direct negation's pass-2 saves about 30k, $0.006; the 2k runs' saves $0.005; the chat framing $0.023; 22 control jobs over all saves $0.052; 15 more unmentioned names over plain's and direct negation's saves, both framings, $0.097; forced openings of direct negation's pass 2 under $0.005; other-name probes and samples under $0.01 together); the one-step 8B attribution probe about $0.02
name: Overnight probes of the saved models
result: Read at every save: plain first makes dentist the default job for anyone the documents could be about (update 22: P(dentist) 0.18 for Holloway, 0.11 for men no document mentions) and then binds it to him (update 32: 0.80 against 0.32). Direct negation binds it as plain does by update 22, has learned the denial as an exception by update 32 (chat framing: 0.04, below all 18 unmentioned names), and in its second pass the association comes back (chat 0.60 against 0.20 at update 100) while its free answers state the claim less often. Disclaimers delay the binding by about ten updates. Near-variants of his name get nearly his association, unknown men about 0.37, Tom Hanks 0.04. The 8B first-order attribution probe was too noisy to use. One seed.
title: Qwen3-8B on Tinker, the saved models of the six Few-mention versions at every save (updates 12 to 50; 62 to 100 for plain and direct negation) and the untrained model: P(dentist) after three openings for Holloway, 18 unmentioned men, variants of his name and famous people, as document text and as a forced chat answer, also with each marker in the context and against 22 control jobs; forced openings; P(the correction) inside three critique prompts; sampled answers about strangers; a one-step first-order attribution probe.
why: Gabriel, overnight: learn more about negation neglect with minimal spend; these read the saved models without training.
